gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's US store prices, which change the budget pick and the mechanical-parts pick: Revopoint's store lists the INSPIRE 2 (0.05 mm) at $384, only $25 above ChatGPT's $359 budget pick, the Creality Ferret Pro (0.1 mm, sized for objects 15 cm to 2 m). Creality's own store lists the blue-laser CR-Scan Raptor at $879, $20 under the infrared-only CR-Scan Otter at $899.
standout_why: Two rival pages were compared. 3dprinting.com/3d-scanners/ (cited) dates its prices to 2026-06-01 and lists INSPIRE 2 ~$549, Raptor ~$1,499, Seal ~$699, MINI 2 ~$829, Einstar 2 ~$1,249 and VEGA ~$1,999. 3dprinting.com small-format (cited) uses prices from 2026-05-28 to 06-01 and lists POP 3 Plus ~$619, MINI 2 ~$829, Seal ~$699 and Moose ~$699. Both pages show the Ferret Pro about $190 cheaper than the INSPIRE 2. Neither has today's prices, which put the INSPIRE 2 within $25 of the Ferret Pro and the Raptor below the Otter. Neither page prices spray, markers or turntables either. ChatGPT's own cards for POP 3 Plus ($619) and MINI 2 ($929) are also above today's store prices ($526 and $663).
decides: Budget pick: at today's prices the Ferret Pro loses to the INSPIRE 2. For $25 more the INSPIRE 2 has twice the stated accuracy (0.05 vs 0.1 mm), and Creality pitches the Ferret Pro at 15 cm to 2 m objects, which is wrong for small printable parts. Mechanical-parts pick: the Raptor at $879, with 7 blue laser lines, beats the Otter ($899, infrared only) on both price and shiny or dark parts, so the Otter row on our page loses its reason to exist. Small-detail pick: ChatGPT's MINI 2 at $929 is now $663, but the 3DMakerpro Seal (0.01 mm) lists at $419, so the MINI 2 loses on price unless a reviewer number shows it scans better. Caveat: the Revopoint and 3DMakerpro prices come from each store's product search feed, which may show the lowest-priced variant. I could not confirm the Standard-edition prices one variant at a time because both stores returned HTTP 429. Re-check before publishing.
